title: Tennis
description: Test your knowledge of aces, slams, and rallies!

questions.question: How many Grand Slam tournaments are held each year?
questions.explanation: The 4 Grand Slams are Australian Open, French Open, Wimbledon, and US Open.

questions.question: Which Grand Slam is played on clay?
questions.explanation: The French Open at Roland Garros is the only Grand Slam played on red clay.

questions.question: In tennis scoring, the score after 'love' is '15'.
questions.explanation: Tennis scoring goes love, 15, 30, 40, then game.

questions.question: Who holds the record for most men's Grand Slam singles titles?
questions.explanation: Novak Djokovic holds the men's record with 24 Grand Slam singles titles.

questions.question: Who has won the most women's Grand Slam singles titles in the Open Era?
questions.explanation: Serena Williams has 23 Grand Slam singles titles in the Open Era.

questions.question: A 'love game' is one where the loser scores zero points.
questions.explanation: A love game is won without the opponent winning a single point.

questions.question: What is the term when a server wins a point with an unreturnable serve?
questions.explanation: An ace is a legal serve that the opponent fails to touch.

questions.question: Rafael Nadal is famous for his dominance on which surface?
questions.explanation: Nadal is called the 'King of Clay' for his record 14 French Open titles.

questions.question: How many sets does a man typically need to win a Grand Slam match?
questions.explanation: Men's Grand Slam matches are best-of-5, so 3 sets are needed to win.

questions.question: A tiebreak is typically played to 7 points, win by 2.
questions.explanation: Standard tiebreaks are first to 7, with a margin of 2 required.
